slides.0.title: Cahors and the Lot and Garonne valleys
slides.0.subtitle: Home of the "black wine" Malbec and neighbouring Fer country
slides.1.title: The Cahors rules
slides.1.highlights.0.title: AOC and varieties
slides.1.highlights.0.content: AOC in 1971; red only; at least 70% Malbec with Merlot and Tannat each allowed up to 30%; at least 4,000 vines per hectare (Wine With Seth, Wikipedia)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Scale
slides.1.highlights.1.content: About 4,200 ha; around 25% exported, and exports doubled between 2004 and 2013 (Wine With Seth)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Style
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Wine Folly: plum, tobacco and a touch of green apple; Wine With Seth: wines from the plateau and upper terraces can develop over a decade or more
slides.1.content: White and rosé from the same land can only be sold as IGP Lot.
slides.2.title: The black-wine story
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Medieval fame
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Cahors wine was served at the 1152 wedding; in the 13th century Cahors traders shipped wine to England via Bordeaux, and the "black wine" later went on to Russia (Wine Folly, Wikipedia)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: The 1956 frost
slides.2.highlights.1.content: The February 1956 frost left almost all vineyards needing replanting, after which Malbec became more dominant (Wine With Seth)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: The Argentine link
slides.2.highlights.2.content: In 2007 the UIVC partnered with the Argentine wine agency; 17 April is World Malbec Day (Wine With Seth)
slides.2.content: Malbec is an old local variety in Cahors, not a newcomer.
slides.3.title: Upstream on the Lot: Marcillac
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Marcillac at a glance
slides.3.highlights.0.content: A VDQS in 1965 and an AOC in 1990; about 200 ha, of which 161 ha are planted; about 20 km northwest of Rodez in the Aveyron (Wikipedia)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Red clay
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Soils are iron-oxide-rich red clays called rougiers; terraced steep slopes face due south with about 2,200 sunshine hours (Wikipedia)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Mansois
slides.3.highlights.2.content: The main variety is Mansois (the local name for Fer Servadou), about 90%; the style is light with raspberry notes, usually drunk within two years (Wikipedia)
slides.3.content: Here Fer shows a lighter side than Cahors.
slides.4.title: Garonne valley: Buzet and Marmandais
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Buzet
slides.4.highlights.0.content: A VDQS in 1953 (Côtes de Buzet), an AOC in 1973 and renamed Buzet in 1986; about 1,800 ha across 27 communes in Lot-et-Garonne (Wikipedia)
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Buzet varieties
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Reds use Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Côt and Merlot; whites use Muscadelle, Sauvignon and Sémillon (Wikipedia)
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Côtes du Marmandais
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Upgraded from VDQS to AOC in 1990; southeast of the Entre-Deux-Mers along the Garonne; 12 varieties including Abouriou and Fer (Wikipedia)
slides.4.content: These are Bordeaux satellites, stylistically the closest to Bordeaux.
